"Using composition change with bipartite networks will give an error message

Since I'm actually using sparse bipartite networks with composition change

fixed it or whether the problem wasn't there before and you signaled it.
Can you please elaborate on that?

Thanks. Regards,
Marco

messages.body_plain:
Dear Marco,

I noticed that some of the code to deal with composition change in 
bipartite networks is missing, so I added the error message to alert 
users. I had not heard of any problems, but it is probably not obvious 
that the code is incomplete.

If you have missing values with sparse _format_ networks I would have 
expected the code to be very slow. (I fixed the one-mode sparse missings 
recently because the method was hopelessly slow with a significant number 
of missing data, and I was working with such a network.) (If it worked, 
this part would be OK, I think.)

I will try to deal with this asap, as soon as I have investigated the 
dyadic covariates from yesterday's messages!

Regards,

Ruth

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Testing time heterogeneity
messages.body_plain:
Dear Ruth,

I am having problem with SIENA's new feature, testing time heterogeneity.


I followed the Manual and ran, as a test, its example. It worked just fine. I then tried to run same analysis with my model (a model for the co-evolution of network and behavior, 83 actors (including structural zeros, no missing data), 4 waves - the model converges just fine, no problem). I keep on receiving the following error message:



"Error in G[, , 1:nEffects] <- moment :   number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length"

I tried to simplify my model (less parameters, only three waves). Same problem appears.

I also tried to directly specify the time dummies but I got the following error message:

"Error: could not find function "includeTimeDummy""

Thanks in advance for your help!

C?cile

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Testing time heterogeneity
messages.body_plain:
Dear Cecile,

If you cannot find the function includeTimeDummy I suspect your 
RSiena/RSienaTest is not the latest version.

It is in R-forge revision 88 and onwards in RSienaTest and revision 96 and 
onwards in RSiena. The Windows binary for the latter is not yet available 
on R-forge, but that for RSienaTest revision 88 is. You will need to be 
running R version 2.11.0 or later.

Regards,

Ruth

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] Two RSiena points
messages.body_plain:
Hello Ruth & Tom,

teaching creates a certain pressure to do things ... I've been teaching 
two days of network evolution modeling with RSiena here in Lexington, 
Ky, so I had to abandon the old Siena 3 platform, at least for a while, 
but it is addictive. As Josh may already have written you, we 
encountered two mistakes that you should know of:

    * there is a letter '0' missing in line 170 of the R Script that is
      on Tom's website, together with the s50 data. The script reads "aa
      <- matrix(nrow=5, ncol=2)" while the number of rows must be 50.

    * the siena01Gui() call is futile because currently you cannot
      specify any models. If you want to, instead of opening the
      fix(effects) screen, you get the error message "Error in
      `[.data.frame`(name, , priorityColumns) : undefined columns
      selected". Josh suspected that this may have something to do with
      the new time heterogeneity test.

As I will be teaching another course in ~10 days, I would appreciate it 
very much if these points could be repaired. For the script, I obviously 
can do that myself... but not for the Gui. We will work with scripts in 
the first place, but nonetheless I want people to see how (and THAT) the 
Gui works as well. At some moment in the coming days, I need to send the 
zipped R packages we will work with to the student assistant managing 
the final software distribution (I think they use CDs)...

By the way, Maarten - if you read this - we had no problems with 
'sienaModelCreate' during the workshop. What you report sounds weird...

Thanks & Greetings,
Christian

messages.body_plain:
Dear Chip,

As far as I know, the value 10 is interpreted as a structural zero indeed in RSiena, without the need for any further things to be done. I suggest that you just try it out and call print01Report; then the structural zeros will be reported. If this does not work as expected, please send another message!

Best wishes,

Tom

An alternative is the stable release of CRAN (dating from March 15). Ruth is away for holidays for one more week, so it is better to assume that there will be no new version on R-Forge within the coming days.

I shall add the 0 to the Rsienascript - this will be changed when there is a further update to this file. Note that at the Siena Scripts webpage I now have added dates for files, so you can see immediately when there is a new version.

Best regards,

Tom

messages.subject: [Rsiena-help] coding missings
messages.body_plain:
Dear Chip,

Maybe your networks are data frames not matrices. (try 
class(friend.data.w1) to find out, and 
friend.data.w1 <- as.matrix(friend.data.w1)
to change it.

Ask again if this is not the problem.

Regards,

Ruth
